lesson.intro: Una clausula de relativo anade informacion sobre un sustantivo. La gran division: defining (especificativa) dice de que persona o cosa hablamos - es esencial y va sin comas; non-defining (explicativa) anade un dato extra que se podria quitar - va entre comas y nunca con that.

sections.heading: 1 - Defining vs non-defining
sections.body:
Defining: informacion esencial para saber de quien/que se habla. Sin comas. Se puede usar that. Si se quita, la frase pierde sentido o cambia.

Non-defining: informacion extra que se puede quitar. Entre comas. Nunca that. En el habla se marca con pausas.
examples: The man who called you is my boss. (defining)
Mr Lee, who called you, is my boss. (non-defining)
Students who cheat will fail. (solo los que copian)

sections.heading: 2 - Pronombres relativos
sections.body:
• who - personas
  • which - cosas y animales
  • that - personas o cosas (solo defining)
  • whose - posesion (personas y cosas)
  • where - lugar   when - tiempo   why - razon (tras the reason)
examples: the colleague who helped me
the film which / that we saw
the man whose car was stolen
the town where I was born

sections.heading: 3 - Relativo como sujeto u objeto
sections.body:
Si el relativo es el sujeto del verbo de la clausula, no se puede omitir: The man who lives here.

Si es el objeto, en clausulas defining se puede omitir: The man (who) I met. A esa clausula sin relativo se le llama contact clause.
examples: The book that is on the table is mine. (sujeto - no se omite)
The book (that) I lent you is mine. (objeto - se puede omitir)
The song I like best is old. (sin relativo)

sections.heading: 4 - Cuando usar 'that' y cuando no
sections.body:
that solo en clausulas defining. En non-defining: who / which.

that es la opcion preferida tras superlativos y tras all, everything, nothing, the only, the first.
examples: It's the best film that I've seen.
It's the only thing that matters.
My car, which is red, is outside. (non-defining: nunca 'that')

sections.heading: 5 - Preposiciones en relativas
sections.body:
Informal: la preposicion va al final: the person who I spoke to.

Formal: preposicion + whom / which al principio: the person to whom I spoke.

No se pone preposicion delante de that ni de who. Con phrasal verbs, la preposicion se queda al final.
examples: The people I work with are nice. (informal)
The colleagues with whom I work are nice. (formal)
the house I live in / the house in which I live

sections.heading: 6 - Non-defining: comas y 'which'
sections.body:
Comas obligatorias antes y despues. Nunca that. Nunca se omite el pronombre.

which puede referirse a toda la oracion anterior: He was late, which annoyed me.
examples: My laptop, which I bought last year, has broken.
Sarah, who works with me, is getting married.
She passed the exam, which surprised everyone.

sections.heading: 7 - whose / where / when / why y relativas reducidas
sections.body:
whose + sustantivo = posesivo (his/her/its + sustantivo). where = lugar (= in/at which). when = tiempo. why = razon (the reason why).

Relativas reducidas: who is/are + -ing → solo -ing (the people living here); which was/were + participio → solo el participio (the letter sent yesterday).
examples: The author whose book won the prize is here.
That's the restaurant where we had dinner.
I remember the day when we met.
The man standing over there is my boss.

sections.heading: 8 - Elegir la relativa correcta
sections.body:
Personas → who / that / whose. Cosas → which / that / whose. Lugar → where. Tiempo → when.

Informacion esencial → sin comas, cabe that, se puede omitir si es objeto. Informacion extra → con comas, who / which, no se omite.
examples: The woman who lives here is a vet.
Rome, which I visited last year, is stunning.
This is the best book that I've ever read.

contrast.title: Defining vs non-defining
rows: The book that I bought is good.
This book, which I bought, is good.

mistakes: NO: My father, that is a teacher, is retired. -> SI: My father, who is a teacher, is retired.
NO: The keys who I lost were new. -> SI: The keys which / that I lost were new.
NO: The man who he lives here is nice. -> SI: The man who lives here is nice.
NO: This is the house which I was born. -> SI: ... the house where I was born / which I was born in.
NO: The person to who I spoke... -> SI: The person to whom I spoke... / who I spoke to...
NO: Paris which is the capital of France is nice. -> SI: Paris, which is the capital of France, is nice.
NO: She's the best friend what I have. -> SI: She's the best friend (that) I have.
